rendered: The document does not support the premise. It reports that prestraining raised the Li-ion diffusion coefficient of the V2O5 films, not lowered it. The abstract states an an increase of the diffusion coefficient of lithium ions by up to 2.5-times[1] with elastic prestrains below 2%[2]. The strained-to-unstrained diffusion coefficient ratios in Fig. 5[3] are all above unity, rising to about 2.5[4] at the largest strain. The authors attribute the increase to geometry: an out-of-plane compressive strain produces in-plane tensile strains which effectively increase the total[5] volume of the crystal. They also suggest the increase could be due to a reduction of ion migration barriers under imposed mechanical strain. So the document gives no reason for a decrease and no decreasing factor. The factor it reports is an increase of up to 2.5[6] times.
